article.title: The PEG word-form grammar
article.para:

This appendix reproduces the formal definition of Lojban's word-forms: the morphology section of the parsing expression grammar (PEG) that current Lojban parsing software implements. It is the precise statement of the rules presented informally in
and : which strings of letters constitute cmevla, cmavo, and brivla, where words begin and end, and which letter sequences are permitted at all.

The grammar is the one used by the camxes parser family, at the revision pinned for this edition's verification work; it is the work of Jorge Llambias (la .xorxes.). Every rule below is reproduced exactly as that file defines it, but the file itself is a plain-text program, and this appendix is typeset for reading: each rule is set out under its own name, the arrow that separates a rule's name from its definition is written → where the file writes <- , the rules are grouped under headings, and the explanatory comments carried in the file appear here as ordinary prose. Nothing in a rule's definition has been changed, reordered, or omitted.

PEG morphologystatus of
This grammar is the de facto standard definition of Lojban's word-forms, implemented by current software; the consonant-glide-vowel ban within it is separately committee-approved. For the full authority history, see .

A parsing expression grammar differs from more familiar grammar notations in one crucial way: the choice operator / is ordered. When several alternatives are given, the first one that succeeds is taken, and the rest are never tried. Together with the lookahead operators & (the following material must be present) and ! (the following material must be absent), this makes the grammar deterministic: any stream of Lojban sounds is divided into words in exactly one way.

listitem.para: A rule has the form name → expression: the construct called name is parsed by that expression.
Concatenation is written by juxtaposition, with no operator between the parts.
/ is ordered choice, as described above.
? makes the element to its left optional; * allows it to repeat any number of times, including none; + requires at least one. Repetitions take as much as they can.
& requires what follows it to be present, and ! requires it to be absent; neither consumes any text.
. stands for any character, [] for a class of characters, and text in quotation marks for itself.
An italic note such as #: PUSH after a rule is a directive to the implementation, not part of the rule; the ZOI rules explain the ones used here.

section.title: Words and ZOI quotes
section.para: The grammar's entry point is a text: a sequence of words, each optionally followed by a pause. The three rules that follow classify one word.

Pure PEG cannot handle ZOI quotes, because it cannot check whether the closing delimiter is the same as the opening one. ZOI quote handling is the only part of Lojban's grammar that needs mechanisms external to the pure PEG grammar to be implemented properly; those mechanisms are implementation-specific. The four rules below therefore carry implementation directives, shown in italics: the opening delimiter is remembered (PUSH), the quoted text must differ from it (PEEK-DIFF), and the closing delimiter must equal it (POP-EQ).

section.title: cmevla
section.para: The source file also carries, as comments, an earlier formulation of the cmevla rules in terms of a cmevla_syllable and a doi_la_lai_lahi guard; the rules above supersede it.
